sections.html: Orange County sits in the Hudson Valley with Goshen as its seat. Its three cities are Middletown, Newburgh and Port Jervis, and the rest is split into 20 towns with a scattering of villages. About 417,669 people lived here as of July 2025, up 4.1% since 2020, in 138,608 households. The median owner-occupied home is worth $387,900 and median gross rent is $1,680.

sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Orange County?
sections.html:
Town, county and special district bills are mailed by the town and paid to the town collector without penalty during the collection window. Delinquent amounts and penalties go to the county Department of Finance, now on the third floor of the County Building at 255 Main Street in Goshen. The county's page lists 845-291-2480 for questions.

Three cities are carved out. The county does not collect or enforce taxes inside Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis, so owners there deal with the city directly. Properties outside those cities but inside the Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis school districts pay current school tax to the district and only pay the county once the bill turns delinquent.

Usual collection windows
TaxCollectedPaid to
County and townJanuary through MarchTown collector
SchoolSeptember through NovemberSchool district
VillageJune through October (a few villages start earlier)Village

Delinquent school tax from outside-city parcels reaches the county in March for Middletown, April for Newburgh and November for Port Jervis, on the county's calendar.

The county takes possession of parcels for unpaid tax through a foreclosure once a year, and the parcels are then offered at a public auction. A booklet with general information and the list of parcels is available from the Real Property Tax office before the sale.

Parcels that do not sell go onto a leftover list that used to be open for bids each month, but that deed sale process is paused because of recent changes to New York's Real Property Tax Law. Bids on the leftover list require official bank checks or money orders and a 10 percent deposit, not cash.

The county also posts surplus and non-surplus reports for the 2024 and 2025 auctions and the 2025 leftover list, which follow the state's Article 11 changes. Anyone claiming surplus funds should consult an attorney. A seller who is behind should ask Finance how far the foreclosure has gone before choosing between paying, selling and waiting.

Assessments in Orange County are set by the town or city assessor, so complaints go to the local board of assessment review. State law opens those hearings on the fourth Tuesday of May unless a local law sets another date, so check the date with your assessor. If the board leaves the value unchanged, Small Claims Assessment Review is the lower-cost court route for most homeowners, and a tax certiorari case in State Supreme Court is the route that calls for an attorney.

The county's parcel search lets you look up owner, assessed values, tax maps, photos and comparable sales for any parcel, and it is useful before a grievance and before pricing a sale. For state relief, the STAR credit is registered through the State Tax Department's Homeowner Benefit Portal, and a seller should close that registration at the sale.

sections.h2: What changes if my house is inside a village or a city?
sections.html:
A village adds its own bill. Owners in a village pay current and late village tax to the village itself up to October 31, so a village balance is not something to settle at the county office. Most villages mail bills in June, while South Blooming Grove and the Village of Kiryas mail in January and Cornwall-on-Hudson and Washingtonville mail in March.

City owners have their own offices. The county's collection page lists the City of Middletown at 845-346-4150, the City of Newburgh at 845-569-7330 and the City of Port Jervis at 845-858-4014. Each city's school district sets its own dates as well, and the three districts publish their own phone numbers for tax questions.

For a sale, this means several balances may sit on one house, such as town and county, village or city, and school. Ask the closing attorney to request each payoff separately, and match every figure to the day of closing so nothing is left behind on the next bill.

Work out which collector holds the balance. In a town, current bills sit with the town collector until the window closes and then move to the county Department of Finance. In Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis, call the city.

  • Ask for a payoff figure in writing, with the date it is good through.
  • Ask whether foreclosure has started on the parcel.
  • Give the figure to your attorney so it is paid at closing.
  • Close your STAR registration if you receive that benefit.

A buyer paying cash can purchase the house as it is, with the lien, any repairs and any tenants. Whichever route you pick, the payoff is deducted from what you receive, so knowing it before you accept an offer tells you what you will actually take home.

sections.h2: From unpaid bill to closing, step by step
sections.html:
The order of events in Orange County is predictable, which helps if you are deciding how fast to move.

  1. The town collector takes the bill without penalty during the window, which for county and town tax runs January through March.
  2. Once the window closes, unpaid county and town tax moves to the Department of Finance in Goshen along with penalties.
  3. If it stays unpaid, the county can foreclose, and parcels it takes are offered at the yearly public auction.
  4. Parcels that do not sell land on the leftover list.

A sale at any point before foreclosure is complete lets the payoff come out of your proceeds. Bring the latest bill, your parcel number, and any notice from the county or city when you call for the figure. Ask the person on the phone to put it in writing, and confirm the date it is good through, because interest and penalties keep running on a delinquent balance.

faqs.q: Where do I pay delinquent property tax in Orange County, NY?
faqs.a: Delinquent county and town tax goes to the Orange County Department of Finance, on the third floor of the County Building at 255 Main Street in Goshen. The number on the county's pages is 845-291-2480. Inside the cities of Middletown, Newburgh and Port Jervis the county does not collect, so call the city.

faqs.q: When are Orange County property tax bills collected?
faqs.a: Collection periods vary by town, but county and town tax is generally collected January through March, school tax September through November and village tax June through October. Your own bill states the dates that apply, and your municipality's collector can confirm them.

faqs.q: Is the Orange County tax auction happening now?
faqs.a: The county's auction page currently shows no tax delinquency auctions scheduled. It also says the leftover list deed sale is paused because of changes to state tax law. Sign up for the page's email alerts or ask the Real Property Tax office for updates.

faqs.q: What can I do if I think my Orange County assessment is too high?
faqs.a: File a complaint with your town or city board of assessment review, which meets starting the fourth Tuesday in May unless a local law sets another date. If that fails, Small Claims Assessment Review is open to most homeowners. Call your assessor first, since an informal talk can fix errors.

faqs.q: Can I sell my house in Orange County before foreclosure?
faqs.a: Yes. The county can only auction a parcel once foreclosure is complete, and a sale that pays the full tax lien at closing clears the debt. Ask Finance for a written payoff and which stage your parcel has reached, and do not wait for an auction notice.
